problem.title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network with Step Transportation Cost and Fixed Shipment Charge
problem.description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. At each plant, a manager decides how many units to produce each period subject to a per-period production capacity. Produced goods add to plant inventory; a per-unit holding cost is charged for every unit stored at a plant at each period end. From each plant, goods are shipped to warehouses over established lanes (a sparse arc set). Each arc offers quantity-discount pricing: the per-unit shipping cost decreases as the shipment volume moves into higher volume tiers, and each shipment dispatched on an arc incurs a fixed charge. An arc has a fixed shipment size (e.g. truck capacity), so the number of dispatches required in a period equals the ceiling of total flow divided by shipment size. Total fixed cost for an arc in a period is therefore fixed_cost_per_shipment times the number of shipments. Warehouses carry inventory across periods at a per-unit holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity constraint. From each warehouse, goods are forwarded to retailers over another sparse set of established lanes, each with the same tier-based pricing and multi-shipment fixed-charge structure. Each retailer has a deterministic demand per period that must be exactly fulfilled. The goal is to choose production quantities, inter-tier shipments, tier selections, shipment counts, and ending inventory levels to minimize total cost: production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, variable tier-based shipping costs on all arcs, and total fixed shipment charges across all arcs and periods.
problem.objective_description: Total cost: production costs at plants, inventory holding costs at plants and warehouses, variable per-unit tier shipping costs (summed over active tier flows), and total fixed shipment charges (fixed_cost_per_shipment times number of shipments) on all plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-retailer arcs, summed across all valid arcs and periods

constraints.description: Plant inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory at plant i equals initial inventory plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses in period t0
Plant inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory at plant i in period t equals ending inventory in the previous period plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses
Warehouse inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory at warehouse w equals initial inventory plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers in period t0

Warehouse inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory at warehouse w in period t equals ending inventory in the previous period plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers
Production at each plant in each period must not exceed the plant's per-period production capacity
Inventory held at each warehouse at the end of each period must not exceed the warehouse's storage capacity
For each retailer and period, total inflow from all connected warehouses must exactly equal the retailer's demand
The total flow on each plant-to-warehouse arc equals the sum of flows across all tier variables for that arc and period
The total flow on each warehouse-to-retailer arc equals the sum of flows across all tier variables for that arc and period
On each plant-to-warehouse arc, at most one pricing tier can be active per period
On each warehouse-to-retailer arc, at most one pricing tier can be active per period
Flow in each tier on each plant-to-warehouse arc must be at least the tier's lower bound times the tier's activation indicator
Flow in each tier on each plant-to-warehouse arc must be at most the tier's upper bound times the tier's activation indicator
Flow in each tier on each warehouse-to-retailer arc must be at least the tier's lower bound times the tier's activation indicator
Flow in each tier on each warehouse-to-retailer arc must be at most the tier's upper bound times the tier's activation indicator

decision_variables: produce[i,t]: units produced at plant i in period t (continuous, non-negative)
inventory_plant[i,t]: inventory held at plant i at end of period t (continuous, non-negative)
inventory_wh[w,t]: inventory held at warehouse w at end of period t (continuous, non-negative)
flow_pw[i,w,t]: total units shipped from plant i to warehouse w in period t (continuous, non-negative, valid arcs only)
flow_wr[w,r,t]: total units shipped from warehouse w to retailer r in period t (continuous, non-negative, valid arcs only)
flow_pw_tier[i,w,tier,t]: units shipped in pricing tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w) in period t (continuous, non-negative, valid arc-tier combinations only)
flow_wr_tier[w,r,tier,t]: units shipped in pricing tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r) in period t (continuous, non-negative, valid arc-tier combinations only)
active_tier_pw[i,w,tier,t]: binary indicator that arc (i,w) uses pricing tier in period t
active_tier_wr[w,r,tier,t]: binary indicator that arc (w,r) uses pricing tier in period t
num_shipments_pw[i,w,t]: integer number of dispatches on arc (i,w) in period t (total flow <= shipment_size * num_shipments)
num_shipments_wr[w,r,t]: integer number of dispatches on arc (w,r) in period t
parameters: prod_cost[i]: production cost per unit at plant i
prod_capacity[i]: maximum units that can be produced at plant i in any single period
hold_cost_plant[i]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at plant i
initial_inv_plant[i]: inventory held at plant i at the start of the planning horizon
hold_cost_wh[w]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at warehouse w
wh_capacity[w]: maximum inventory units that can be stored at warehouse w at end of any period
initial_inv_wh[w]: inventory held at warehouse w at the start of the planning horizon
demand[r,t]: units required by retailer r in period t, which must be exactly fulfilled
tier_lb_pw[i,w,tier]: lower bound on flow volume for pricing tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w)
tier_ub_pw[i,w,tier]: upper bound on flow volume for pricing tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w)
tier_cost_pw[i,w,tier]: per-unit shipping cost in pricing tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w)
tier_lb_wr[w,r,tier]: lower bound on flow volume for pricing tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r)
tier_ub_wr[w,r,tier]: upper bound on flow volume for pricing tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r)
tier_cost_wr[w,r,tier]: per-unit shipping cost in pricing tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r)
fixed_cost_pw[i,w]: fixed charge per dispatch on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w); total fixed cost = fixed_cost_pw * num_shipments_pw
fixed_cost_wr[w,r]: fixed charge per dispatch on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r); total fixed cost = fixed_cost_wr * num_shipments_wr
shipment_size_pw[i,w]: maximum units per dispatch on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w); flow <= shipment_size_pw * num_shipments_pw
shipment_size_wr[w,r]: maximum units per dispatch on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r)
problem.additional_notes: This is a Mixed Integer Program (MIP). Arc topology is defined by the fixed_cost tables (rows define valid arcs). Each arc has a shipment_size (truck/batch capacity). The number of dispatches in a period is the integer variable num_shipments_pw/wr, and total flow must not exceed shipment_size * num_shipments — this forces num_shipments to equal ceil(flow/shipment_size) at optimality. Total fixed cost for an arc is fixed_cost_per_dispatch * num_shipments. The tier selection constraint (flow_pw_tier_select) restricts at most one pricing tier to be active per arc per period, ensuring volume-based pricing is applied to the total flow rather than allowing simultaneous tier mixing. Combining tier-specific per-unit costs with flow tier variables linearizes what would otherwise be a nonlinear quantity-discount cost function.

produce.label: production_quantities

inventory_plant.description: Inventory held at plant i at end of period t
inventory_plant.label: plant_inventory

inventory_wh.description: Inventory held at warehouse w at end of period t
inventory_wh.label: warehouse_inventory

flow_pw.description: Total units shipped from plant i to warehouse w in period t along a valid arc
flow_pw.label: plant_to_warehouse_flow

flow_wr.description: Total units shipped from warehouse w to retailer r in period t along a valid arc
flow_wr.label: warehouse_to_retailer_flow

flow_pw_tier.description: Units shipped in pricing tier tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w) in period t
flow_pw_tier.label: plant_to_warehouse_tier_flow

flow_wr_tier.description: Units shipped in pricing tier tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r) in period t
flow_wr_tier.label: warehouse_to_retailer_tier_flow

active_tier_pw.description: 1 if arc (i,w) uses pricing tier tier in period t; 0 otherwise
active_tier_pw.label: plant_to_warehouse_tier_active

active_tier_wr.description: 1 if arc (w,r) uses pricing tier tier in period t; 0 otherwise
active_tier_wr.label: warehouse_to_retailer_tier_active

num_shipments_pw.description: Number of dispatches on arc (i,w) in period t; flow_pw <= shipment_size_pw * num_shipments_pw
num_shipments_pw.label: plant_to_warehouse_shipment_count

num_shipments_wr.description: Number of dispatches on arc (w,r) in period t; flow_wr <= shipment_size_wr * num_shipments_wr
num_shipments_wr.label: warehouse_to_retailer_shipment_count
